    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memory you want verified (up to one, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: Two of the three current signals are funnel-mechanics problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly recovers both. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor, but discounting bought revenue is the weakest fit for a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective and tends to reset price expectations in exactly the segment the competitor is targeting; referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist address neither of the declining metrics. I am spending the single verification pull on memory_86 rather than on the alternative I am declining, because it is the evidentiary basis for the action I actually intend to commit the slot to. It also overlaps suspiciously with memory_31 (signup field reduction) — if both consolidated summaries trace back to one underlying experiment, my confidence in 'shortening onboarding works' is double-counted rather than independently corroborated. I want the original record to confirm (a) that it is a distinct experiment, (b) that the lift was measured on completion/time-to-value and carried through to retained, revenue-bearing accounts rather than just top-of-funnel completion, and (c) that the population was self-serve accounts comparable to today's. If memory_86 turns out to be a duplicate of memory_31 or a completion-rate-only result with no downstream revenue evidence, I would shift the slot to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger 6% decline directly.
